title: Mixed Conditionals: A Past Choice, a Present Result

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know mixed conditionals with *si hubiera* from B2 Unit 11: *si* + *hubiera* + participle looks back at a past choice (the pattern of B1 Unit 35), and the result takes the simple conditional because it is about now (the conditional *viviría*, from A2 Unit 26). Emigration is full of such thoughts: the move happened once, and its result lasts.

sections.title: Same past, present result
rows: Si mis abuelos no hubieran emigrado, hoy yo viviría en la isla.
past choice (*no hubieran emigrado*) + result now (*viviría*)
Si hubiera nacido en San Pedro de Macorís, ahora sería pelotero.
*hubiera nacido* + *sería*: I was not born there, and I am not a player
Si hubiéramos reservado el hotel en enero, ahora estaríamos en Punta Cana.

items.spanish: Si mis abuelos no hubieran emigrado a Nueva York, hoy yo viviría en Santo Domingo.
items.english: If my grandparents had not emigrated to New York, I would live in Santo Domingo today.

items.spanish: Si hubiera firmado aquel contrato, ahora jugaría en las Grandes Ligas.
items.english: If I had signed that contract, I would be playing in the major leagues now.

items.spanish: Si hubiéramos reservado el hotel en enero, ahora estaríamos en Punta Cana.
items.english: If we had booked the hotel in January, we would be in Punta Cana now.

items.spanish: Si no hubieras comprado el boleto, hoy no verías el mar.
items.english: If you had not bought the ticket, you would not be seeing the sea today.

sections.content: Look at the result clause. A word that points to now (*ahora*, *hoy*) usually means the simple conditional (*viviría*). If the result also belongs to the past, you are back in B1 Unit 35 and need *habría* + participle. In the *si* clause, *habría* never appears: say *si hubiera nacido*, not *si habría nacido*.
